newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU to look into German post office freight pricing.
newsitem.headline: EU to look into German post office freight pricing.

text.p: The European Commission is investigating the German post office for "predatory pricing" allegedly aimed at eliminating competing package delivery companies, the Commission's competition watchdog confirmed on Monday.

In a letter to Deutsche Post AG (DPAG), the Commission said it intended to take a "negative position" on a complaint that the German postal service illegally offsets parcel rates with high rates for letter mail.
"On the basis of preliminary assessment, we believe that DPAG has engaged in unlawful predatory pricing," the Commission wrote.
It added that the use of cross-subsidised rates over the last 12 years "indicated an intention by DPAG to eliminate its competitors."

A spokesman confirmed that Deutsche Post had received the letter. "This is only one step toward a decision by the EU," a Deutsche Post spokesman told Reuters. "The EU has not reached a final ruling yet."
The Commission said Deutsche Post covered losses in freight delivery, where it faces competitors, with unnecessarily high rates for letter mail. DPAG holds a legal monopoly on letter delivery.

United Parcel Service, a package carrier based in the United States, filed the complaint in 1994. The Commission said it would hear objections from DPAG this spring, and could reach a decision by next autumn.
